annotations.text:
Tacet mobile — batch one
The shell, Home (A6 Digest) and Orders (A1 Worklist), derived from tacet-desktop-patterns.md v4.6 rather than patched from the current phone build. Light Paper shown; dark is a token swap only.

Sample data is the app's own (RT-…047, Chen Meiling, ¥312), retimed to the English US formats §1.18 requires.
What changes vs the live phone chrome: red count badges → one 6px Sage dot · brass active tab → Ink 500 · 10px/800 labels → 13px Inter 500 sentence case · uppercase sheet headings → sentence case.

The unseen card replaces the "NEW" pill: --td-unseen surface + inset 4px Sage edge, settling to Paper over 600ms on open. Inset shadow, never a border — an indicator that resizes its row makes the list jump.

One Dusk element: the header's New order. The FAB is gone — a floating circle is not in the system, and §1.7 puts the primary in the header.

The drawer, on a phone. Pinned block is exactly two rows: identifier + ONE status pill, then the action row — 3 controls at this width (state action · workhorse · ⋯), with the workhorse holding the right edge.

Actions are Secondary: the sheet inherits the page's Dusk budget, and Orders already spent it. The Dusk here is the auto-routed badge — tacet acting, which is exempt.

Every page ships all six states. Loading has no status line and no chip counts — a real number is not known yet, and §1.7's honesty rule forbids inventing one. Empty and no-results are different sentences: one is a compliment, the other is a search that missed.
Batch two — Customers and Products, the other two Worklists. Same vocabulary as Orders: chips on the primary axis, records as cards, the drawer as a sheet with a two-row pinned header.

No status line, deliberately: 693 records, none waiting on anyone (§1.7's work rule — Customers is its reference case).

The pulse takes its line render. Four tiles cannot share a 390px row, and showing two of them would be an arbitrary subset.

Tier pills are neutral. A tier is a fact about the customer, not a state needing attention — Sage and Amber are not spent on it. Blocked keeps Brick, because that one IS a state.

The unseen surface means nobody on the team has opened this record — one shared timestamp, not "you haven't". It appears on Customers and Orders, where records ARRIVE, and never on Products, which the merchant authored. Same card vocabulary, different truth.

The sage "New" pill stays removed: signing up today and being unopened are different facts.

Products carries the sub-view strip under the header — Catalogue · Stock activity · Categories, Ink underline on the live one. It swaps what kind of thing you are looking at; the chips below narrow the same records.

No status line here either: the chips already say running low and out of stock, and §1.7 prefers the fact nothing else shows over a fourth copy of a count.

The hybrid (§1.13). An order is glance-and-act, so its sheet is the whole story. A product is light to glance at and heavy to edit, so its sheet carries exactly one extra door — Open full page — and nothing else about it differs. Two zoom levels of one record, not a second pattern.

Synced with what shipped in /m (the phone build), 22 Aug.

Four things changed on contact with the product, all the same kind: the design promised something the phone could not do yet.

· Orders and Products head with an EMPTY Dusk slot — neither create flow exists on a phone, and a primary that only says "do this on the desktop" is a promise the page cannot keep. §1.7 says the empty slot is the finished answer.
· Tier chips carry no counts. No endpoint returns them, and an invented number is worse than a missing one.
· The customer record is read-only: every figure on it is one the server already computes, and none of the write flows exist here yet. The action row lands with them.
· Home's Today carries the four figures the dashboard actually returns, with their deltas.
Batch three — Inbox, Delivery and Sales: the three archetypes the phone had not proved yet. A Worklist behind a sub-view strip, a Console, and a Board.

One fact, one place: the work waiting is in the status line, so the pulse slot stays empty rather than saying it twice.

A review that nobody has opened wears the unseen surface, exactly as an order does — a review ARRIVES. "Replied" stays a pill because that one is a state the operator put it in.

Send reply is Secondary. Writing a reply is the operator acting, and Dusk means one thing: tacet did this for you. Do not correct this to a Dusk button.

A Console, so no Dusk anywhere: configuring is not the AI acting.

No master switch — delivery cannot be turned off, and promoting Holiday mode into that slot would say it can. It sits in Timing with its consequence spelled out ("Off. Orders are being accepted."), which is what the master-switch rule is really asking for.

The automation row carries a breathing Dusk dot and states what it did today. An automation indicator is exempt from the one-Dusk rule; it is reporting, not asking.

A switch is Dusk only where it arms an automation; a plain preference takes Ink. Same rule as everywhere else, applied to a control that did not have one.

The Board is the status — five cards, one dot each, at most two metrics, one link out. No summary banner over them: it would be a fourth copy of what the dots already say.

Eleme keeps its slot while disconnected. An absent channel is information.

The channel detail beside it is the pattern for all three marketplaces: a Console for what you configure, a read-only list under it at full legibility and zero affordance — no chevrons, no actions, the state in italics. Mirrored, never driven.
